hyperedges.label: Race status bar: display wrapper, bar, flags and phase source
Three data sources converge on a single telemetry ingest path
PRO analysis panels are path-dependent across a replay session

nodes.label: spdlog level policy
nodes.rationale: trace/debug off in release, info for life events, warn when work continues anyway, error for a failed operation, critical when the program cannot go on. Never log per-frame or per-packet in a hot loop - it drowns the signal and costs speed. Log events, not the stream.

nodes.label: Track recording from telemetry
nodes.rationale: A tracker-equipped vehicle drives one lap; the client records the trajectory, closes the loop and smooths it with a spline.

nodes.label: D6: CSV import holds the whole file as strings
nodes.norm_label: d6: csv import holds the whole file as strings
nodes.rationale: CsvTable::rows is a vector<vector<string>> of every cell - 1.6 million std::string for an hour of 25 Hz logging. The binding dialog only needs column names and a dozen rows; the rest could be read in a second pass during conversion.

nodes.label: RaceDisplay wrapper
nodes.rationale: High-level wrapper owning initialization, screen-resize handling and render orchestration, so callers do not touch the status bar internals.

nodes.label: RaceFlags / FlagColor
nodes.rationale: Flag colour management: FlagColor enum (Green, Yellow, Red, Blue, White, Checkered), colour-to-RGBA conversion, and left/right flag state.

nodes.label: RaceStatusBar
nodes.rationale: Top-of-screen race session bar: OpenGL-drawn background, borders and flags, with text drawn separately on the ImGui foreground draw list to keep the two rendering concerns apart. Not thread-safe by design - UI thread only.

nodes.label: Race flags (green / yellow / red / finish)
nodes.rationale: Flags can be raised locally or synchronised from the server.

nodes.label: Automatic phase detection from ModeManager
nodes.rationale: The bar reads GetPhaseLabel() and GetPhase() straight from ModeManager and derives the left flag colour from the phase (Yellow for Practice, Green otherwise), so no duplicate flag state has to be kept in sync.

nodes.label: Responsive scaling from a 1600x900 reference
nodes.rationale: Base geometry (256x25 bar, 16x16 flags, 0.5x text) is defined at 1600x900 and scaled by the average of scaleX and scaleY, with minimum clamps on border (1px) and spacing (2px), so one layout covers XGA through 4K without per-resolution tuning.

nodes.label: A1: SECTORS panel still computes sectors from the sample log
nodes.norm_label: a1: sectors panel still computes sectors from the sample log
nodes.rationale: ProSectors calls zoneTimes(samples...) - the method LapTypes.h explicitly declares abandoned because log density depends on FPS and playback speed, part of the log belongs to an unplayed portion during replay, and with an incomplete log the sector boundary is not found at all. Timing moved to crossing-timestamp differences in RaceManager while SECTORS did not, so one screen holds two implementations of the same quantity.

nodes.label: Pro::AnalysisLap (operator-selected lap)
nodes.rationale: The lap the operator explicitly chose, as opposed to m_current_lap_number where the playhead happens to sit; GRAPHS and LAP LIST follow it, the other analysis panels do not.

nodes.label: B2: TRACK REPORT and SECTORS ignore the operator-selected lap
nodes.norm_label: b2: track report and sectors ignore the operator-selected lap
nodes.rationale: ProTrackReport and ProSectors read v.m_current_lap_number (where the playhead sits) while GRAPHS and LAP LIST read Pro::AnalysisLap() (what the operator picked). Move the slider inside another lap and the screen shows two different laps at once with no sign they differ. Either every analysis panel follows AnalysisLap or none does.

nodes.label: D3: SECTORS scans all vehicles and all samples every frame
nodes.norm_label: d3: sectors scans all vehicles and all samples every frame
nodes.rationale: A loop over g_vehicles calling zoneTimes on each vehicle's best lap, under the vehicles mutex, every frame, with no cache; cost grows with both car count and lap length. It also binds auto& instead of const auto& on a read-only pass.

nodes.label: Invariant: timing anchored to source timestamps, not frames
nodes.norm_label: invariant: timing anchored to source timestamps, not frames
nodes.rationale: Lap and sector times are computed from utc_elapsed_ms rather than deltaTime, which is exactly why a live session and its replay produce identical numbers; any edit that reintroduces deltaTime into time computation silently destroys this.

nodes.label: B1: event log is built by observation, not from the recording
nodes.norm_label: b1: event log is built by observation, not from the recording
nodes.rationale: ProEvents keeps file-level statics (s_log, s_prev, s_sessBestLap, s_leader) and only creates an event when a rendered frame happens to catch the state change. Seek past a lap and its events never exist; open another recording and the old events remain because replay_close knows nothing about panels. This contradicts the very principle VehicleJournal was introduced for.

nodes.label: B3: laps roll back on seek, sectors do not
nodes.norm_label: b3: laps roll back on seek, sectors do not
nodes.rationale: restore_keyframe restores lap state from the snapshot but deliberately leaves sector state 'as played' (documented in ReplayPlayer.h). The consequence is the same as B1: sector times at the same point in the recording can differ from what the operator saw a minute ago, so the invariant 'one point in the recording, one picture' does not hold everywhere.

nodes.label: B5: panel state survives a change of recording
nodes.norm_label: b5: panel state survives a change of recording
nodes.rationale: replay_close drops vehicles, session and device bindings but knows nothing about panel statics (s_analysis_lap, s_display_vehicle, s_view_min, s_view_span, s_log). The panels are not at fault: the replay module simply has no 'the recording changed' event for them to subscribe to.

nodes.label: C4: LapData::telemetryPoints is a dead field copied everywhere
nodes.norm_label: c4: lapdata::telemetrypoints is a dead field copied everywhere
nodes.rationale: The vector is never filled anywhere in the tree, yet LapData is copied into the snapshot every frame, into every keyframe, into the journal and into GetVehicleLapsCopy - each copy constructs and destroys an empty vector.

nodes.label: D1: snapshot copies every lap of every vehicle each frame
nodes.norm_label: d1: snapshot copies every lap of every vehicle each frame
nodes.rationale: PublishSnapshot assigns view.laps = vehicle.m_laps inside the loop over g_vehicles, on every Update and every seek step - a std::map with a node per lap and a vector inside each node, roughly 800 allocations per frame for values that have not changed since the last lap.

nodes.label: Shared data must be protected
nodes.rationale: Any variable written by one thread and read by another is either behind a std::mutex or passed through a thread-safe queue; there is no such thing as a merely shared variable between threads.

nodes.label: Invariant: panels read the published snapshot
nodes.norm_label: invariant: panels read the published snapshot
nodes.rationale: Where implemented, panels read the published snapshot rather than live vehicles, so they cannot catch a half-finished rebuild.

nodes.label: Prefer a queue to a mutex
nodes.norm_label: prefer a queue to a mutex
nodes.rationale: The network thread puts a finished snapshot in a queue and the render thread takes it, so the threads never touch the same memory at once - races are impossible by construction, which is cleaner than sprinkling mutexes. Locks that do exist are held as briefly as possible, never across heavy work.

nodes.label: pending-consume hand-off pattern
nodes.rationale: Network/serial threads never touch OpenGL; data crosses into the render thread as a pending item consumed there (e.g. server track geometry) because GPU upload must happen on the context thread. Shared data otherwise sits behind mutexes such as g_track_mutex and points_mutex.

nodes.label: B4: one frame after a seek, position and timing disagree
nodes.norm_label: b4: one frame after a seek, position and timing disagree
nodes.rationale: main.cpp calls RaceManager::Update before replay_apply_pending_seek, so crossings queued in m_pending_crossings are parsed only by the next Update; during the seek only PublishPositionsOnly runs, leaving new positions with stale lap numbers, timers and table. One frame is small, but every derived 'car is on this lap' cue (LapTrace::at_playhead, LAP LIST row highlight) blinks in that window.

nodes.label: C2: replay_journal returns a raw pointer into a mutating map
nodes.norm_label: c2: replay_journal returns a raw pointer into a mutating map
nodes.rationale: The pointer is valid 'until the replay closes' only because every participant currently lives on the render thread; g_journal.clear() in replay_close/build_journal would dangle every panel's pointer at once. A shared_ptr<const VehicleJournal> would cost one shared_ptr per frame and end the question.

nodes.label: C6: journal warm-up blocks the frame with no sign of life
nodes.norm_label: c6: journal warm-up blocks the frame with no sign of life
nodes.rationale: build_journal replays the entire recording synchronously on the render thread. Invisible on a 2.7 MB / 288 s file, but linear in length: an hour-long race with a full field freezes the window for seconds on open, with no progress indicator and no way to cancel - the only trace is a console line printed afterwards.

nodes.label: C7: journal duplicates vehicle history in memory
nodes.norm_label: c7: journal duplicates vehicle history in memory
nodes.rationale: journal.lap_samples[lap] = session.samples copies every sample of every vehicle while Vehicle::laps still holds the live history, so replay telemetry sits in memory twice - roughly 2 x 21 MB for an hour with five cars now that LapInfo has grown to ~120 bytes. A side effect of snapshotting the journal by copy rather than a deliberate design.

nodes.label: D2: LAP LIST copies the lap list and immediately discards it
nodes.norm_label: d2: lap list copies the lap list and immediately discards it
nodes.rationale: GetVehicleLapsCopy is called and then overwritten by journal->lap_times; in replay - the panel's main mode - that first copy is never needed, and the journal check costs one map lookup and could come first.

nodes.label: VehicleJournal (replay recording journal)
nodes.rationale: Exists precisely because a lap list that loses everything after the playhead is useless for post-race analysis; it holds the whole recording independent of where the operator has looked.

nodes.label: OpenGL calls only from the context thread
nodes.norm_label: opengl calls only from the context thread
nodes.rationale: Every gl* call happens on the thread that created the context; the network thread never touches GL.

nodes.label: RAII
nodes.rationale: The foundation of memory safety here: a resource opened in an object is released in its destructor even when an error occurs, so nobody has to remember to close it.

nodes.label: Smart pointers over raw pointers
nodes.rationale: unique_ptr by default (exactly one owner), shared_ptr only when there really are several owners because it costs more, raw T* only as a non-owning view that is never deleted. Manual new/delete leaks whenever an exception escapes between them.

nodes.label: Invariant: keyframes without sample history
nodes.rationale: Snapshots exclude sample history, which makes them cheap enough for a 250 ms keyframe interval and near-instant rollback.

nodes.label: Explicit ownership in design
nodes.rationale: For every object you must be able to say who owns it and when it dies; if you cannot answer, the design is not ready and it is too early to write code.

nodes.label: GPU resources need their own RAII wrapper
nodes.norm_label: gpu resources need their own raii wrapper
nodes.rationale: Smart pointers do not manage OpenGL textures and buffers, so they are wrapped in a class whose constructor calls glGen* and destructor glDelete*; this directly closes video-memory leaks.

nodes.label: A3: telemetry export does not survive UTC midnight
nodes.norm_label: a3: telemetry export does not survive utc midnight
nodes.rationale: time_s is computed as (utc_ms - first_utc_ms)/1000 while utc_ms counts milliseconds from midnight, so a session running 23:50 to 00:10 jumps -86400 s mid-file and the CSV time axis runs backwards. CsvImport already handles the midnight wrap explicitly - the same module, two different rules.

nodes.label: A4: CSV import time origin can stay zero
nodes.norm_label: a4: csv import time origin can stay zero
nodes.rationale: have_first_time is set even when to_number fails, so a corrupt time cell in the first coordinate row leaves first_time at zero and a SecondsFromStart recording is offset from zero instead of its real start.

nodes.label: A2: GPS fix type labelled against the protocol
nodes.norm_label: a2: gps fix type labelled against the protocol
nodes.rationale: Protocol.h says fix_type 4 = RTK_FIXED, but ProChannels maps 5 -> RTK Fixed and 4 -> RTK Float, so a real recording with fix=4 is displayed as Float. This is exactly the number that decides whether centimetre accuracy can be trusted, and there is currently no source of truth - the tracker firmware must arbitrate.

nodes.label: C1: two locking idioms on one mutex
nodes.norm_label: c1: two locking idioms on one mutex
nodes.rationale: VehiclesLock is reentrant via a thread_local counter and supports a bulk section that the whole replay rollback rests on, yet ~20 sites take g_vehicles_mutex with a raw lock_guard. It works today only because both live on the render thread and never overlap; a single raw lock_guard added to the packet-ingest path would self-deadlock on the first rollback and present as a hang with no stack. A mutex that has a wrapper with semantics must never be taken bare.

nodes.label: C3: backward seek holds the vehicles mutex, forward seek does not
nodes.norm_label: c3: backward seek holds the vehicles mutex, forward seek does not
nodes.rationale: Backward rollback takes enter_vehicles_bulk_section so readers see only 'before' and 'after', but forward feed_range locks and unlocks per packet inside ingest, exposing thousands of intermediate states on a one-minute jump. The asymmetry is explained neither by a comment nor by the code - it is either intentional and undocumented, or an oversight.

nodes.label: D5: settings written to disk on every wheel click
nodes.norm_label: d5: settings written to disk on every wheel click
nodes.rationale: saveScales() and saveVis() open, rewrite and close pro_scales.ini directly in the input handler, so ten wheel clicks are ten file writes; a debounced or on-exit write is the obvious fix.

nodes.label: Review severity scale A/B/C/D
nodes.rationale: A = shows wrong numbers or loses data (an engineer will decide on a lie); B = behaviour depends on how the operator reached that point, so the analysis is not reproducible; C = architectural debt that the next edit will break; D = performance, dead code, noise.

nodes.label: VehiclesLock (reentrant bulk-section lock)
nodes.rationale: Reentrant through a thread_local counter and offering enter_vehicles_bulk_section, so a reader waits and sees only the 'before' and 'after' of a rollback; freezing individual consumers pointwise did not solve that.

nodes.label: DataSource abstraction (ServerSource / LocalReceiverSource)
nodes.rationale: The rest of the code works against DataSource and never learns which concrete source is underneath, so adding a third source is a new class and nothing else changes.

nodes.label: Minimal header surface
nodes.rationale: Only what is actually used from outside goes in the .hpp; the less that is exposed, the freer the internals are to change without breaking callers.

nodes.label: One function, one job
nodes.rationale: A function doing three things cannot be reused or tested; the tell is that you cannot name it with one verb, or the name wants an 'and' (parse_and_send).

nodes.label: Expected failures return optional / expected
nodes.rationale: A corrupt packet, a missing GPS fix or an unreachable server is normal life, not an exception. Returning std::optional/std::expected forces the caller to check, whereas a sentinel like -1 silently flows into the calculation.

nodes.label: Validate inputs at the public entry point
nodes.norm_label: validate inputs at the public entry point
nodes.rationale: A public function checks its arguments first (buffer length before reading, non-null pointers) so the rest of the code can trust its data.

nodes.label: Vehicle focus selection (P key)
nodes.rationale: P cycles three states: start ID entry, cancel entry, or reset g_focused_vehicle_id to -1 (leader tracking). Edge detection via a wasPPressed static because GLFW reports held keys as PRESS every frame.

nodes.label: Multi-digit vehicle ID entry
nodes.rationale: Digits accumulate into a string confirmed by ENTER so IDs like 12 or 345 are reachable, unlike a single-keypress scheme; per-digit press latches prevent one keypress from appending repeatedly.

nodes.label: COM / serial data source (SX1280 LoRa receiver)
nodes.norm_label: com / serial data source (sx1280 lora receiver)
nodes.rationale: Ports are discovered automatically on a background thread; packet format is shared with the server through rajagp_core's RajaParser.

nodes.label: Dual-edge track creation
nodes.rationale: Driving the left edge and then the right edge yields a track with real borders, unlike single-lap telemetry recording which only gives a centre line.

nodes.label: RAJAGP Client (Windows desktop app)
nodes.rationale: C++17 / OpenGL 3.3 (glad) + GLFW + Dear ImGui timing and telemetry client for RC-car and karting races.

nodes.label: rajagp_core shared protocol library
nodes.rationale: Client compiles Crc.cpp and RajaParser.cpp straight out of the sibling closed RAJAGP Server repo so client and server share exactly one packet format; the build fails without that neighbouring directory.

nodes.label: Built-in simulator data source
nodes.rationale: Generates vehicles on the loaded track so the app can be exercised without hardware.

nodes.label: Telemetry ingest pipeline (processIncomingTelemetry -> g_vehicles)
nodes.rationale: Three independent data sources (COM/serial, Track Server WebSocket, simulator) converge into one pipeline so there is exactly one implementation of vehicle-state assembly.

nodes.label: Track Server WebSocket data source
nodes.rationale: Deliberately built on native WinHTTP instead of a third-party socket library so it works on ARM64; owns a reconnecting connection thread and tracks channel quality (loss, jitter).

nodes.label: .trk2 binary track format
nodes.rationale: Header plus two polylines with UTM georeferencing via GeographicLib, stored in saves/tracks/; the same track can also arrive from the server in chunks.

nodes.label: Roles and admin tokens (Networking -> Accounts)
nodes.rationale: user/admin roles selected by the token entered on connect; the admin controls the race and issues 1-hour / 1-day / permanent access tokens, copyable by click.

nodes.label: Built-in simulator
nodes.rationale: Generates vehicles on the track for testing without hardware.

nodes.label: Dual-edge track creation (README)
nodes.rationale: Drive the left edge, then the right edge, producing a track with real borders stored as binary .trk2 (header plus two polylines, UTM georeferencing via GeographicLib).

nodes.label: Ground receiver (LoRa to USB COM)
nodes.rationale: Ground module that receives radio packets from trackers and hands them to the client over a USB COM port.

nodes.label: Hotkeys (F1, Shift+C, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+wheel, Esc)
nodes.norm_label: hotkeys (f1, shift+c, ctrl+s, ctrl+p, ctrl+wheel, esc)

nodes.label: Inno Setup installer
nodes.rationale: Packs x64\Release (exe plus all DLLs including the VC++ CRT), assets and a Mesa3D fallback for software OpenGL on VMs/RDP/old GPUs, and installs the VC++ Redistributable when needed; paths inside the script are relative and output lands in installer/out/.

nodes.label: Local mode (COM port, no server)
nodes.rationale: The SX1280/LoRa receiver plugs straight into the PC; ports are auto-discovered in the background and picked from a menu, so no server is required.

nodes.label: Network mode (Track Server over WebSocket)
nodes.rationale: Native WinHTTP WebSocket - chosen without third-party socket libraries specifically so it also runs on ARM64; the server supplies track geometry, vehicle states and authoritative timings while the client watches packet loss and jitter.

nodes.label: PRO mode (Pit Wall floating panels)
nodes.rationale: A separate screen of floating panels (Laptime, Lap List, Lap Info, Sectors, Track Map, G-Force, Channels, Events) with layout locking and per-panel text zoom (Ctrl+wheel); channel scales persist in pro_scales.ini and layout in imgui.ini.

nodes.label: RAJAGP Client (this repository)
nodes.rationale: Operator application: track and vehicle visualization, lap and sector timing, race control and the Pit Wall PRO screen. Published by RAJAGP SIA, version 1.1.

nodes.label: RAJAGP Server (Track Server)
nodes.rationale: Closed repository that receives tracker telemetry, computes authoritative positions and laps, serves clients over WebSocket, and hosts the shared rajagp_core protocol library.

nodes.label: OpenGL track visualization
nodes.rationale: OpenGL 3.3 track map (asphalt, kerbs, 20 m grid) with a zoom/rotate/inertia camera, plus real-time vehicles with motion interpolation, name labels and a timeout for vanished trackers.

nodes.label: Tracker (onboard ESP32 + GPS/RTK transmitter)
nodes.rationale: On-vehicle module collecting coordinates and telemetry and transmitting them over LoRa (SX1280) radio.

nodes.label: Recommended fix order (A2, A1, A3/A4, B2, C1, B1/B5)
nodes.norm_label: recommended fix order (a2, a1, a3/a4, b2, c1, b1/b5)
nodes.rationale: A2 first because it is cheapest and is lying right now about trust in the data; then A1 (a panel using an algorithm this same repo declares unfit); then the two silent-lie time bugs; then B2 to unify AnalysisLap usage; then C1 as protection against a hang that cannot be debugged; then a 'replay changed/seeked' event to replace immortal statics.

nodes.label: Invariant: one ingest path for all sources
nodes.norm_label: invariant: one ingest path for all sources
nodes.rationale: Replay feeds ingest_wire_packet - the same entry point as the live receiver - so no second lap-counting implementation exists; that is the main reason the replay can be trusted. Foreign packets during replay are cut off at a single point rather than per source.

nodes.label: Exceptions caught at module boundaries
nodes.rationale: Exceptions are allowed in the desktop client and track_server, but they are caught at module boundaries so one broken packet is logged and dropped instead of killing the process. The module boundary is a wall: an error inside the packet parser becomes an optional/expected or is caught there.

nodes.label: Unidirectional dependency arrows
nodes.rationale: rajagp_core knows nothing about client or track_server; both depend on core but not on each other, and there are no cycles. The moment core needs to know something about the client, the design has slipped.

nodes.label: Focus target existence check under g_vehicles_mutex
nodes.norm_label: focus target existence check under g_vehicles_mutex
nodes.rationale: The entered ID is looked up in g_vehicles under a lock_guard before g_focused_vehicle_id is set, so the camera never latches onto a vehicle that does not exist; a missing ID is reported and the mode exits.

nodes.label: 10-second focus input timeout
nodes.rationale: FOCUS_INPUT_TIMEOUT measured against glfwGetTime cancels a half-typed ID so the app cannot get stuck swallowing digit keys if the operator walks away mid-entry.

nodes.label: ARM64 dev build target
nodes.rationale: ARM64 is the fast local dev target on this Windows-on-ARM machine; x64 previously crashed with 0xc000007b because vcpkg deps were only installed for the arm64 triplet and arm64 DLLs were picked up.

nodes.label: Server timings are authoritative
nodes.rationale: RaceManager computes laps, sectors, deltas and positions locally for COM/simulator, but when connected to Track Server the server's timings overwrite the local calculation; serverPosition == 0 marks a local session.

nodes.label: Coordinate frame conventions (txt / trk2 / sim, render offset)
nodes.norm_label: coordinate frame conventions (txt / trk2 / sim, render offset)
nodes.rationale: The conventions are subtle, so anything positional must be checked against src/rendering/Render.* and TrackEditor before changing.

nodes.label: Local UI state files excluded from git
nodes.norm_label: local ui state files excluded from git
nodes.rationale: imgui.ini, pro_scales.ini, pro_panels.ini, ui_scale.ini, recent_files.txt and devices.db are per-machine state, so they are written next to the working directory and never committed.

nodes.label: No automated tests or linter
nodes.rationale: The project has no autotests and no linter, so correctness rests on code review and the coding standard rather than CI.

nodes.label: x64 distribution target
nodes.rationale: installer/installer.iss packages x64\Release specifically, so x64 must be rebuilt before regenerating the installer even though daily dev happens on ARM64.

nodes.label: C5: sample rate declared in two places
nodes.norm_label: c5: sample rate declared in two places
nodes.rationale: RaceManager's kTelemetrySampleInterval = 0.1f and TelemetryExport's SAMPLE_RATE_HZ = 10.0 are unconnected; the second is written into the MoTeC CSV header, so changing the first makes the exported file lie silently. Only one side even carries a comment.

nodes.label: const by default, careful auto, named constants
nodes.norm_label: const by default, careful auto, named constants
nodes.rationale: const tells the reader nothing changes here; auto only where the type is obvious from the right-hand side; magic numbers become named constants (len < PACKET_SIZE_BYTES); variables are initialised at declaration because uninitialised ones cause bugs that are hard to catch.

nodes.label: Naming convention (snake_case / PascalCase / UPPER_CASE / trailing _)
nodes.rationale: A name says what a thing is, not what type it is; the trailing underscore on private fields immediately distinguishes object state from a local. Units belong in the name (timeout_ms, lap_time_seconds) because that is cheap and kills a whole class of bugs.

nodes.label: TODO / FIXME / HACK markers
nodes.rationale: Uniform, greppable labels so both humans and AI agents can find unfinished work: TODO = finish later, FIXME = works but badly, HACK = temporary crutch with the reason spelled out.

nodes.label: Comments explain why, not what
nodes.rationale: What the code does is visible in the code - if it is not, rewrite the code rather than adding a comment. Every public function carries a short block: what it does, takes, returns, and what happens on error.

nodes.label: Code is read ten times more often than written
nodes.norm_label: code is read ten times more often than written
nodes.rationale: The governing principle above every other rule: write for the person opening the file a year from now with no memory of it. Formatting is out of scope - .clang-format handles it automatically.

nodes.label: English-only identifiers and console output
nodes.rationale: The project builds without /utf-8, so Cyrillic in narrow string literals becomes '?' at compile time; SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8) in main.cpp fixes display only, not compilation. Runtime data (track and device names from SQLite, paths) is not a literal and passes through correctly.

nodes.label: Device registry (SQLite devices.db)
nodes.rationale: SQLite-backed registry of tracker names/groups in src/core/DeviceRegistry; it is why sqlite3 is a hard dependency of both triplets.

nodes.label: sqlite3 required for both vcpkg triplets
nodes.norm_label: sqlite3 required for both vcpkg triplets
nodes.rationale: The device registry database needs sqlite3; missing it in either triplet breaks link or startup. sqlite3.dll is applocal-deployed next to the exe and swept into the installer by the *.dll wildcard.

nodes.label: AppPaths single source of data directories
nodes.norm_label: apppaths single source of data directories
nodes.rationale: Everything the app writes lives under one saves/ root (tracks, results, replays, logs). Paths are declared once in core/AppPaths.h and never spelled as string literals in new code; AppPaths::prepare() runs first in main to create the tree and migrate the old layout (src/saves, race saves, logs).

nodes.label: Project knowledge graph (graphify-out)
nodes.rationale: Holds god nodes, community structure and cross-file relationships so codebase questions return a scoped subgraph instead of raw grep output.

nodes.label: graphify query / path / explain
nodes.rationale: Preferred entry point for codebase questions: returns a scoped subgraph that is usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: graphify update (AST-only refresh)
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code to keep the graph current; AST-only so it costs no API calls.

nodes.label: graphify skill registration
nodes.rationale: Registers the /graphify trigger so the skill at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md is loaded before any other action on that command.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Read only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context - it is large.

nodes.label: graphify wiki index
nodes.rationale: Used for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing when it exists.

nodes.label: OpenGL/src module layout
nodes.rationale: core / input / logging / network / racing / rendering / track / ui / vehicle, with src as the single header root so files can move between directories without rewriting neighbours' includes.

nodes.label: src as single #include root
nodes.rationale: $(ProjectDir)src is the only header root, so there are no relative ../.. includes. Not cosmetic: while paths were file-relative, moving any file broke its neighbours' includes and the same header was spelled three different ways.

nodes.label: Legacy UI.cpp de-duplication
nodes.rationale: UI.cpp/UI_Elements.cpp used to live at project root while identically named empty stubs sat in src/ui outside the build, so editing 'the' file changed nothing. The stubs and the name collision are gone - there is exactly one file.

nodes.label: D4: dead constants in ProGraphs
nodes.rationale: CHANNEL_COUNT and MIN_SEEK_SECONDS are declared and used nowhere; MIN_SEEK_SECONDS even carries a three-line comment describing behaviour that does not exist in the code.

hyperedges.label: Race status bar: display wrapper, bar, flags and phase source
Three data sources converge on a single telemetry ingest path
PRO analysis panels are path-dependent across a replay session
